newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Hypo-Bank unit says managed funds up 37 pct.
newsitem.headline: German Hypo-Bank unit says managed funds up 37 pct.

text.p: Total funds under management at Allfonds International Asset Management, the fund management arm of Munich's Hypo-Bank, increased 37 percent to 21 billion marks in 1996, the group said on Thursday.
This represents an increase of 5.6 billion marks in the year to the end of 1996, said Josef Wertschulte, executive board member of Hypo-Bank and chairman of the administrative council of Allfonds.
Allfonds was established in 1996 to merge the consultancy, development and marketing-to-institutions businesses of Hypo-Bank's asset management interests into one unit.

Hypo-Bank said that investment management was one of its strategic priorities and that altogether the Hypo group had assets totalling 96 billion marks under management, of which 65 billion marks came from institutional business.

Allfonds said that it hoped to expand its business further through cooperation with its partner in the U.K., Foreign & Colonial (F&C) and its U.S. asset management partner Massachusetts Financial Services (MFS).
Wertschulte said that around 80 percent of funds were bond-backed funds, with 20 percent in equity-backed funds, but said that it expected the amount of equity-backed funds to accelerate quickly.
Allfond said that the changes in German pension fund provision, with an expected shift from state provision to private pension provision, offered tremendous opportunities for the company.
